question: Why can mini-batch noise sometimes help training instead of hurting it?
direct_answer: Because noisy gradients can help the optimizer explore the landscape and avoid overly deterministic, brittle paths.
expanded_answer: Mini-batch gradients are approximate, so their noise makes the updates less perfectly aligned with the full-data gradient. While that adds variance, it can also help the optimizer move out of narrow sharp regions, escape some poor basins, and reduce sensitivity to small local irregularities. In practice, this noise is one reason mini-batch training often generalizes well and is efficient.
key_points: Can help avoid overly sharp or brittle minima
common_wrong_ideas: Noise is always bad and should be eliminated
Mini-batch SGD is inferior because it is less exact
Noise directly improves the model without any tradeoff
